<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.
Hardware: optional single tag without spaces. Use uppercase hardware tags (AMD, NVIDIA, NPU, MI300X), except for exactly these four spellings: Intel, Apple, Huawei, Ascend.
Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
When `--enable-unified-memory` is used with HiCache, host compaction reclaims fragmented space for reuse across sub-pools.

The GPU-side implementation minimizes movement by filling holes with live pages from the boundary being released. The host-side implementation instead repacks live pages in physical order. A single hole near the start of the packing order can therefore cause almost every remaining live page to be copied, even when most pages could stay in place.

These unnecessary copies increase host allocation latency when compaction is required. This PR brings the same minimal-movement strategy to host compaction

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

* Compute the final packed region from the live page count and growth direction.
* Fill only the holes inside that region, using live pages from the boundary being released.
* Leave live pages already inside the final packed region in place.
* Update logical-to-physical and physical-to-logical mappings in place.

For a final packed region containing H holes, the new implementation moves exactly H pages. Physical page order may change, but logical page identities and payloads are preserved.

For example, for an upward-growing pool:

| | Physical page layout | Pages moved |
|---|---|---:|
| Before compaction | `[A, hole, B, C, D]` | — |
| Previous implementation | `[A, B, C, D, free]` | 3 |
| New implementation | `[A, D, B, C, free]` | 1 |

The previous implementation shifts B, C, and D. The new implementation moves only D into the hole, leaving B and C in place while reclaiming the same amount of space.

Both growth directions are supported. The existing synchronization is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

* Existing host-pool unit suite: 46 tests and 43 subtests passed.
* Black and git diff --check passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->


Observed host compaction latency during **GPT-OSS-120B serving with TP=2, unified memory, and HiCache write-back**. Measurements were collected on TP rank 0.

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Average FULL compaction time | 3,970.56 ms | 2.85 ms |
| Average SWA compaction time | 731.39 ms | 0.76 ms |
| Average total compaction time | 4,702.16 ms | 3.71 ms |

These measurements come from separate serving runs and reflect the compaction events observed in each run, rather than a controlled comparison with identical compaction inputs. They measure host compaction latency, not end-to-end serving throughput.

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

-            new_physical_to_logical[target] = logical
+    def _compact_side(self, side: _Side) -> int:
+        # Only fill holes inside the final packed region. Live pages already
+        # inside it stay put; donors come from the boundary being released.
+        # Logical IDs do not require physical pages to preserve their order.
+        grow_up = side.grow_direction == "up"
+        new_watermark = (
+            side.live_page_count
+            if grow_up
+            else side.page_num - 1 - side.live_page_count
+        )
+        step = -1 if grow_up else 1
+        source = side.watermark + step
+        moved_pages = 0
+        for target in sorted(side.free_physical_pages, reverse=not grow_up):
+            if (grow_up and target >= new_watermark) or (
+                not grow_up and target <= new_watermark
+            ):
+                break
+            while source in side.free_physical_pages:
+                source += step
+            logical = side.physical_to_logical[source]
+            source_offset = source * side.page_bytes
+            target_offset = target * side.page_bytes
+            # The destination is a hole and the source is outside the retained
+            # region, so the page slices are disjoint and need no temporary copy.
+            self.raw[target_offset : target_offset + side.page_bytes].copy_(
+                self.raw[source_offset : source_offset + side.page_bytes]
+            )
+            del side.physical_to_logical[source]
+            side.physical_to_logical[target] = logical
+            side.logical_to_physical[logical] = target
+            source += step
+            moved_pages += 1
 
-        side.logical_to_physical = new_logical_to_physical
-        side.physical_to_logical = new_physical_to_logical
         side.free_physical_pages.clear()
-        side.watermark = (
-            len(live) if side.grow_direction == "up" else side.page_num - 1 - len(live)
-        )
+        side.watermark = new_watermark
+        return moved_pages
 
     def _compact(self) -> None:
         events = self._begin_compaction()
